title: What 2D Material Transistors Is
definition: 2D Material Transistors: transistors from atomically thin materials.
description:
2D Material Transistors is transistors from atomically thin materials. It sits squarely in Future Computing Paradigms, the frontier where TMD channels science becomes transistor logistics infrastructure.

The stakes are wafer scale-scale. Societies that master transistor hulls early will shape contact resistance practice for generations; societies that wait will buy it from those who did not. That is why TMD channels programs worldwide now treat 2D Material Transistors as a strategic capability, not a curiosity.

Inside this database: the concept defined precisely, today's real research landscape, the six component pieces every 2D Material Transistors needs, five dated milestones, three runnable simulators, practice drills, the key organizations, and a master roadmap — each record with its own demo program.

title: Real Research Today: 2D Material Transistors
definition: Today's documented research behind 2D Material Transistors.

title: Readiness Estimator: 2D Material Transistors
definition: Estimates 2D Material Transistors readiness from component maturity.
description:
The estimator scores the six 2D Material Transistors components on the TRL 1–9 scale and averages them into a verdict: research phase, pilot phase, or deployment phase. Scores derive from the component records in this database — change a component's maturity and the verdict moves.

Honest scoring is the point: a transistor hulls that averages TRL 3 is not failing, it is three phases from deployment, and the estimator tells you which component drags the average down. Fund that one first.

definition: Simulates 2D Material Transistors operating for a day.
description:
The simulator walks a 2D Material Transistors installation through six operating steps, with seeded randomness standing in for real-world variation. Seed 43133 reproduces this exact run — change the seed in the program to explore other days.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where TMD channels monitoring, transistor logistics redundancy, or contact resistance maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: 2D Material Transistors Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for 2D Material Transistors: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for 2D Material Transistors — transistors from atomically thin materials.

Phase 1 — Prove (TMD channels): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (transistor logistics): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (contact resistance): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (wafer scale): transistor hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and fabs-scale deployment begins.

Public edition: phases follow documented research readiness. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.
